assessments.summary: The proof correctly classifies every nonidentity Euclidean rotation preserving a finite noncollinear subset of Z^2 as a half-turn or quarter-turn. Integer difference matrices force the rotation matrix to be rational; finiteness of the invariant set forces finite order; and the rational algebraic-integer trace argument excludes all finite-order rotation traces except those corresponding to the identity, half-turn, and quarter-turn. The orbit arguments then exclude all nontrivial rotational symmetry at cardinality 153 and exclude quarter-turn symmetry at cardinality 154. At size 154, row and column saturation makes the bounding box [0,76]^2, forcing the center of any preserving half-turn to be (38,38); parity of half-turn orbits excludes that center from S.
scopeQualifications: The result classifies rotations only, not reflections, affine maps, or approximate symmetries.
The 154-point conclusion is conditional on the existence of a no-three-in-line set with nontrivial rotational symmetry; no configuration is constructed.
The proof establishes neither existence nor global nonexistence of 153- or 154-point configurations and leaves 152 <= D(77) <= 154 unchanged.
It does not identify the strict rct4 subclass with the full class of centered half-turn-invariant configurations.
